item.title: Sherlock CI `pull_request_target` Command Injection → GitHub Actions Secret Exfiltration (CVE-2026-44590)
item.description:

Affected Target

Field Value
Software / System sherlock-project/sherlock (GitHub Actions workflow validate_modified_targets.yml)
Versions Affected Commits up to and including pre-fix commit 271608fb (fixed in 6eaec5cc)
Language / Platform Python 3 (PoC), GitHub Actions YAML (target)
Authentication Required No (any GitHub user can open a PR)
Network Access Required Yes

Summary

The validate_modified_targets.yml GitHub Actions workflow in sherlock-project/sherlock uses the dangerous pull_request_target trigger and processes attacker-controlled pull request data (a JSON entry key) in a shell context without sanitization, resulting in command injection. Because pull_request_target runs in the privileged context of the base repository with access to a GITHUB_TOKEN, any external contributor who opens a malicious pull request can execute arbitrary commands in CI, exfiltrate the workflow token, and use it to auto-approve their own pull request — a full supply-chain compromise requiring zero human interaction beyond opening the PR.
